original_question: Fix k >= 2. Does there exist m_0 such that whenever m >= m_0 and G is F_{k,3}-free, then for each residue class l with 1 <= l <= k - 1 and m + k(k+1)/2 == l mod k, the graph G satisfies lambda(G) <= lambda(S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k}), with equality only for that extremal graph?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Conjecture 3.40: the residue-nonzero friendship-graph conjecture for F_{k,3}-free graphs with fixed size.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies the forbidden graph family F_{k,3}, fixes k>=2, uses the right 'for all sufficiently large m' format via an existence statement for m_0, imposes the correct nonzero residue condition 1<=l<=k-1 with m + k(k+1)/2 ≡ l (mod k), names the same candidate extremal graph S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k}, and includes both the spectral-radius inequality and the uniqueness of the extremal graph. Those features match Conjecture 3.40, not the earlier congruence-0 statement.
missing_details: The paper quantifies over G in 𝒢(m,F_{k,3}), i.e. finite, simple, undirected F_{k,3}-free graphs with exactly m edges and no isolated vertices; your draft only says 'G is F_{k,3}-free'.
You need to define the forbidden graph explicitly: F_{k,3}=K_1∨kK_2, the friendship graph consisting of k triangles sharing a common vertex.
You need to define λ(G) as the adjacency spectral radius of G.
You need to define the extremal graph notation S^{1,l}_{n,k}; in the paper, S^{1,l}_{n,k}:=K_l∨((K_{k-l}∨(n-k-1)K_1)∪K_1).
It should be explicit that m_0 depends on k, i.e. m_0=m_0(k).
The variable l should be quantified as an integer satisfying 1<=l<=k-1 and m + k(k+1)/2 ≡ l (mod k), not as a vague 'residue class'.
To be fully stand-alone, it helps to note that under the congruence condition the parameter n=(m-l)/k+(k+3)/2 is an integer, so the graph S^{1,l}_{n,k} is well defined.
The equality clause should use graph isomorphism notation explicitly: equality holds if and only if G ≅ S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k}.
The paper’s ambient graph conventions from the introduction (finite, undirected, simple graphs) are implicit in your draft and should be made explicit if you want a stand-alone formulation.
refined_question: Fix an integer k>=2. Let F_{k,3}:=K_1∨kK_2 be the friendship graph, let λ(G) denote the adjacency spectral radius of a finite simple graph G, and for integers n,k,l with 1<=l<k define S^{1,l}_{n,k}:=K_l∨((K_{k-l}∨(n-k-1)K_1)∪K_1). Does there exist m_0=m_0(k) such that for every integer m>=m_0, every integer l with 1<=l<=k-1 and m + k(k+1)/2 ≡ l (mod k), and every graph G in 𝒢(m,F_{k,3}) (that is, every F_{k,3}-free graph with m edges and no isolated vertices), one has λ(G)<=λ(S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k}), with equality if and only if G ≅ S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k}?
justification: The draft is targeting the paper’s later residue-nonzero refinement for friendship graphs, not the earlier basic friendship conjecture. In Section 3, the survey first defines F_{k,3}=K_1∨kK_2 and states Conjecture 3.28 for the congruence-0 extremal graph K_k∨((m/k)-(k-1)/2)K_1; Theorem 3.38 then confirms that zero-residue case. Immediately afterward, the paper notes that this zero-residue extremal graph is only attainable when m + k(k+1)/2 ≡ 0 (mod k), recalls the nonzero-residue model S^{1,l}_{n,k} from Problem 7/Theorem 3.23, and then explicitly poses Conjecture 3.40 for F_{k,3}-free graphs in the nonzero residue classes. Your draft matches that exact conjecture structure, but it omits the paper’s class notation 𝒢(m,F_{k,3}), the definitions of F_{k,3}, λ(G), and S^{1,l}_{n,k}, and the dependence m_0=m_0(k). Theorem 3.43 is also nearby context because it confirms Conjecture 3.40 for the special case k=2.
